text:
anya (sales): FYI — ACME POC reporting two issues: exported logs in S3 are missing trace IDs so they can't link traces <> logs, and they're seeing intermittent 429s under a simple load test. Can we swarm this?

mike (solutions): Taking point. Lee, can you paste a small log sample and the request headers you saw? Also which export pipeline (fluentd/fluentbit -> Kinesis -> S3?)

lee (acme-customer): thanks. It's fluentd -> s3 via our sidecar. Here's a few lines from the S3 object (redacted):

```
2026-03-20T17:10:03Z INFO request completed method=POST path=/api/v1/generate status=200 latency_ms=120 user_id=12345 request_id=-
2026-03-20T17:10:04Z INFO request completed method=POST path=/api/v1/generate status=200 latency_ms=130 user_id=12345 request_id=-
2026-03-20T17:10:05Z ERROR upstream error status=429 message=rate limit exceeded request_id=-
```

We do set `x-request-id` in the client but it never shows up in the logs.

sam (eng-infra): OK — two things jump out: (1) the ingress / app isn't propagating header into the app log context, and (2) the S3 exporter/buffer might be dropping attributes during transform. Quick checks: are you using the Redwood SDK or a custom client? Also which reverse proxy (nginx/ALB/Envoy)?

lee (acme-customer): custom client (node). ALB in front, then nginx in the pod. We set `x-request-id` client-side.

mike (solutions): Suggested next steps:
1) Ensure request ID header is preserved across ALB -> nginx -> app (ALB should forward headers by default).
2) Make app log include header value (set logger to read `X-Request-Id` / `X-Trace-ID`).
3) Confirm fluentd sidecar isn't normalizing away headers — check parser/filter.
4) Temp rate-limit bump for tenant while we test.

sam (eng-infra): Adding concrete configs. For nginx, add into the log format and proxy_pass headers:

```
# nginx.conf
proxy_set_header X-Request-Id $http_x_request_id;
log_format  main  '$remote_addr - $remote_user [$time_local] "${request}" '
                  '$status $body_bytes_sent "${http_referer}" '
                  '"${http_user_agent}" "${http_x_request_id}"';
access_log /var/log/nginx/access.log main;
```

For a Node app using express, quick middleware to attach header into log context: `app.use((req,res,next)=>{req.id = req.headers['x-request-id'] || uuid.v4(); logger = logger.child({request_id: req.id}); next();})`

mike (solutions): For fluentd -> s3 pipeline, make sure you're forwarding all fields. Example fluentd filter to copy header into record:

```
<filter **>
  @type record_transformer
  <record>
    request_id ${record["headers"] && record["headers"]["x-request-id"]}
  </record>
</filter>
```

If headers are not present in the parsed record you may need to adjust the parser to capture `headers` or use the HTTP input plugin with `keep_time_key` etc.

lee (acme-customer): That makes sense. Where are we changing the exporter config? It's managed in our sidecar chart.

sam (eng-infra): Edit the fluentd configmap in the chart, bump the buffer settings to avoid drops under load:

```
<match **>
  @type s3
  buffer_chunk_limit 8M
  buffer_queue_limit 256
  aws_bucket your-bucket
</match>
```

Also check `flush_interval` and `retry_limit` so 429 bursts don't cause lost records.

mike (solutions): On the Redwood side: we can also surface the trace ID in our console trace view if your requests include `X-Trace-ID` (Redwood supports `X-Trace-ID` or `x-request-id`). Confirm we should look for `X-Trace-ID` or `x-request-id`?

lee (acme-customer): We'll standardize on `X-Trace-ID`.

anya (sales): Quick ask for ops — can we temporarily raise the rate-limit for tenant `acme-corp` in prod-sandbox from 100 req/s to 400 req/s for the next 2 hours while they validate?

deploy-bot: Request logged: ops ticket #OPS-2897 created by anya — awaiting approval.

sam (eng-infra): Ops action is needed. @ops-team please approve OPS-2897 for temporary bump. Meanwhile I'm going to open a short-lived canary to test header propagation: I'll deploy a debug pod with curl that sets `X-Trace-ID` and then tails fluentd output.

mike (solutions): Also adding SDK suggestion for their Node client to guarantee propagation:

```
// before sending request
const traceId = req.headers['x-trace-id'] || uuid.v4();
axios.defaults.headers.common['X-Trace-ID'] = traceId;
```

lee (acme-customer): I pushed a chart change to add `proxy_set_header X-Request-Id $http_x_request_id;` and updated fluentd filter to include `request_id`. Pushing now.

mike (solutions): Nice. Once that's in, reproduce the load test and attach a couple S3 objects that still show missing `X-Trace-ID` if any — paste object key(s) here.

lee (acme-customer): Deployed. Quick smoke shows access logs now include the header and the fluentd sidecar records show `request_id: "abc-123-test"`. I'll run load in 10m and post S3 keys.

sam (eng-infra): Good — additional checklist for us:
- Confirm Redwood console shows trace rows with `X-Trace-ID` (we can correlate by trace id)
- If 429s persist, we need to audit client concurrency and upstream model routing.
- Make sure no PII is being forwarded in headers (reminder for security).

mike (solutions): I'm going to stand by for the S3 keys. If everything looks good we'll close the POC blocker and revert the temporary rate bump. Also I'll prepare a short doc for the customer about best practices for trace propagation and S3 exports.

anya (sales): Thank you all — Lee, ping here when you have the S3 keys. If the rate bump is approved we'll let you know. :thumbsup:

lee (acme-customer): Uploaded two objects: `acme/2026-03-20/part-0003.gz` and `acme/2026-03-20/part-0004.gz`. Both show `request_id` populated now. 429s dropped significantly after bumping concurrency on client side.

mike (solutions): Verified sample from `part-0003.gz` — trace IDs present, and we can correlate with Redwood traces. Looks good from our side.

anya (sales): Ops approved temporary bump and will roll it back at 2026-03-20T20:00Z. Marking blocker resolved pending customer's confirmation.

lee (acme-customer): Confirmed — logs/traces correlated, load test passed. Thanks team!

mike (solutions): Closing thread — will follow up with the short doc + config snippets. :white_check_mark:
